_about: Definitions of Shadowserver reports, written for Looking Glass from the official report pages at https://www.shadowserver.org/what-we-do/network-reporting/ (severity = Shadowserver's own rating of the report). Keys are collection names; IPv6 variants (scan6_*, population6_*, event6_*, device_id6) use the IPv4 entry.

blocklist.title: Block List Report
blocklist.def: Addresses in your network that appear on public block or deny lists run by third parties, gathered into one feed.
blocklist.why: Listed hosts are often sending abuse (spam, login attacks) and may be blocked by others; check what they run.

compromised_iot.title: Compromised IoT Report
compromised_iot.def: IoT devices (routers, cameras and similar) that show clear signs of compromise, detected by means other than web scans, for example honeypot activity.
compromised_iot.why: The device is already under someone else's control: isolate it, reset it and update its firmware.

compromised_website.title: Compromised Website Report
compromised_website.def: Websites that Shadowserver or its partners have verified as compromised, for example with implants, injected code or defacements.
compromised_website.why: Visitors may be infected or redirected; clean the site and find how the attacker got in.

device_id.title: Device Identification Report
device_id.def: Devices fingerprinted in Shadowserver's daily internet scans, classified by vendor, type and model.
device_id.why: An inventory of what is visible from the internet; use it to spot end-of-life or unexpected devices.

event4_honeypot_brute_force.title: Honeypot Brute Force Events Report
event4_honeypot_brute_force.def: Hosts seen by honeypots trying to guess passwords (SSH, Telnet, RDP and other logins).
event4_honeypot_brute_force.why: The host is attacking others, usually because it is infected.

event4_honeypot_ddos_amp.title: Honeypot Amplification DDoS Events Report
event4_honeypot_ddos_amp.def: Amplification DDoS attacks seen by honeypots in which your address was the victim, flooded through other reflecting services.
event4_honeypot_ddos_amp.why: Shows attacks against you, not by you.

event4_honeypot_http_scan.title: Honeypot HTTP Scanner Events Report
event4_honeypot_http_scan.def: Hosts seen scanning web services or trying web exploits against honeypots.
event4_honeypot_http_scan.why: Scanning from your network usually means an infected or misused host.

event4_honeypot_rdp_scan.title: Honeypot RDP Scanner Events Report
event4_honeypot_rdp_scan.def: Hosts seen scanning or attacking Remote Desktop (RDP) on honeypots.
event4_honeypot_rdp_scan.why: Often a step before ransomware attacks; find the scanning process.

event4_honeypot_smb_scan.title: Honeypot SMB Scanner Events Report
event4_honeypot_smb_scan.def: Hosts seen scanning or exploiting Windows file sharing (SMB) on honeypots.
event4_honeypot_smb_scan.why: Typical of worms and infected Windows machines.

event4_initial_access_broker.title: Initial Access Broker Report
event4_initial_access_broker.def: Compromised hosts that are likely controlled by initial access brokers, criminals who sell access to networks.
event4_initial_access_broker.why: Access to this host may be sold to ransomware groups; treat as an incident.

event4_microsoft_sinkhole_http.title: Microsoft Sinkhole HTTP Events Report
event4_microsoft_sinkhole_http.def: Devices that contacted Microsoft's HTTP sinkholes (seized malware domains), shared with Shadowserver by Microsoft.
event4_microsoft_sinkhole_http.why: The device is infected with the named malware.

event4_sinkhole.title: Sinkhole Events Report
event4_sinkhole.def: Connections from infected devices to non-HTTP sinkholes: malware command servers taken over by defenders.
event4_sinkhole.why: The device is infected with the named malware.

event4_sinkhole_dns.title: Sinkhole DNS Events Report
event4_sinkhole_dns.def: DNS lookups for sinkholed malware domains seen from recursive DNS servers. The address is the resolver, not necessarily the infected client.
event4_sinkhole_dns.why: Check the resolver's logs to find the client that asked.

event4_sinkhole_http.title: Sinkhole HTTP Events Report
event4_sinkhole_http.def: HTTP connections from infected devices to sinkholed malware command servers.
event4_sinkhole_http.why: The device is infected with the named malware.

event4_sinkhole_http_referer.title: Sinkhole HTTP Referer Events Report
event4_sinkhole_http_referer.def: Web pages that referred visitors to sinkholed malware domains, pointing to compromised or malicious sites.
event4_sinkhole_http_referer.why: The referring site may be compromised.

event4_honeypot_darknet.title: Darknet Events Report
event4_honeypot_darknet.def: Traffic from your network to unused address space (darknets), typical of scanning and worms.

population_bgp.title: Open BGP Service Report
population_bgp.def: Routers with the BGP routing service (179/tcp) reachable from the internet. This is the population variant of Shadowserver's Open BGP Service report (scan_bgp): every host answering BGP is counted, not only problematic ones.
population_bgp.why: BGP should only accept known peers; restrict it with filters.

population_http_proxy.title: Accessible HTTP Proxy Report
population_http_proxy.def: HTTP proxy servers reachable from the internet (most ask for a password).
population_http_proxy.why: Proxies can be abused to hide attacks; confirm they are meant to be public.

population_isakmp.title: Accessible ISAKMP Report
population_isakmp.def: Hosts with an IPsec VPN key exchange service (ISAKMP/IKE, 500/udp) reachable from the internet.
population_isakmp.why: Usually a VPN gateway; keep it patched, as VPNs are frequent targets.

population_msmq.title: Accessible MSMQ Service Report
population_msmq.def: Windows hosts with Microsoft Message Queuing (1801/tcp) reachable from the internet.
population_msmq.why: MSMQ has had critical remote flaws; it rarely needs to be public.

population_ntrip.title: Accessible NTRIP Report
population_ntrip.def: NTRIP casters (GNSS/GPS correction streaming) reachable from the internet.
population_ntrip.why: Check that access is intended and protected.

scan_adb.title: Accessible ADB Report
scan_adb.def: Android devices with the debugging bridge (ADB, 5555/tcp) open to the internet.
scan_adb.why: Gives full control of the device; close it immediately.

scan_afp.title: Accessible AFP Report
scan_afp.def: Hosts with Apple file sharing (AFP) reachable from the internet.
scan_afp.why: File shares should not be public.

scan_amqp.title: Accessible AMQP Report
scan_amqp.def: Message brokers (AMQP, 5672/tcp, for example RabbitMQ) reachable from the internet.
scan_amqp.why: May expose application data or weak logins.

scan_ard.title: Accessible Apple Remote Desktop (ARD) Report
scan_ard.def: Hosts with Apple Remote Desktop (3283/udp) reachable from the internet.
scan_ard.why: Can be abused for DDoS amplification and leaks system details.

scan_badsecrets.title: Badsecrets Report
scan_badsecrets.def: Web applications using known or very weak cryptographic secrets, often copied from examples.
scan_badsecrets.why: Attackers can forge sessions or run code; replace the secrets.

scan_chargen.title: Open CharGen Report
scan_chargen.def: Hosts running the old Character Generator service (19/udp) on the internet.
scan_chargen.why: Used for DDoS amplification; switch it off.

scan_cisco_smart_install.title: Accessible Cisco Smart Install Report
scan_cisco_smart_install.def: Cisco switches with the Smart Install feature (4786/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_cisco_smart_install.why: Allows taking over the switch configuration; disable the feature.

scan_coap.title: Accessible CoAP Report
scan_coap.def: IoT devices with the CoAP protocol reachable from the internet.
scan_coap.why: Can be abused for amplification and leaks device data.

scan_couchdb.title: Accessible CouchDB Report
scan_couchdb.def: Apache CouchDB databases (5984/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_couchdb.why: Databases should not be public; data may be exposed.

scan_cwmp.title: Open CWMP Report
scan_cwmp.def: Routers with the TR-069 remote management service (CWMP) reachable from the internet.
scan_cwmp.why: Rarely needs to be public and has been exploited by botnets.

scan_ddos_middlebox.title: Vulnerable DDoS Middlebox Report
scan_ddos_middlebox.def: Network middleboxes (such as filters or firewalls) that can be abused to reflect and amplify TCP DDoS attacks.
scan_ddos_middlebox.why: Fix the device configuration to stop it being used in attacks.

scan_dns.title: DNS Open Resolvers Report
scan_dns.def: DNS servers that answer anyone's queries (open resolvers).
scan_dns.why: Used for DNS amplification DDoS; limit recursion to your own users.

scan_docker.title: Accessible Docker Service Report
scan_docker.def: Docker API services reachable from the internet.
scan_docker.why: Gives control of the server's containers.

scan_dvr_dhcpdiscover.title: Open DVR DHCPDiscover Report
scan_dvr_dhcpdiscover.def: Video recorders (DVRs) with a management discovery service (37810/udp) reachable from the internet.
scan_dvr_dhcpdiscover.why: Can be abused for amplification and leaks device details.

scan_elasticsearch.title: Open Elasticsearch Report
scan_elasticsearch.def: Elasticsearch or OpenSearch databases reachable from the internet.

scan_epmd.title: Accessible Erlang Port Mapper Daemon Report
scan_epmd.def: Erlang port mapper (EPMD, 4369/tcp) reachable from the internet, for example from RabbitMQ or CouchDB installations.
scan_epmd.why: Exposes internal services; keep it internal.

scan_exchange.title: Vulnerable Exchange Server Report
scan_exchange.def: Microsoft Exchange mail servers that appear vulnerable, from daily scans.
scan_exchange.why: Exchange flaws are widely exploited; patch at once and check for compromise.

scan_ftp.title: Accessible FTP Report
scan_ftp.def: FTP servers (21/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_ftp.why: FTP sends passwords in clear text; prefer SFTP and check for anonymous access.

scan_gtp.title: Accessible GPRS Tunneling Protocol (GTP) Report
scan_gtp.def: Mobile network GTP services reachable from the internet.
scan_gtp.why: Mobile core services should not be public.

scan_hadoop.title: Accessible Hadoop Report
scan_hadoop.def: Hadoop big-data services reachable from the internet.
scan_hadoop.why: May expose data and allow running jobs.

scan_http.title: Accessible HTTP Report
scan_http.def: Web servers (HTTP on any port) reachable from the internet, with their banners.
scan_http.why: An inventory; look for admin panels and outdated server software.

scan_http_proxy.title: Open HTTP Proxy Report
scan_http_proxy.def: HTTP proxies that relay traffic for anyone.
scan_http_proxy.why: Open proxies are abused to hide attacks; close them.

scan_http_vulnerable.title: Vulnerable HTTP Report
scan_http_vulnerable.def: Web services that appear to have a known vulnerability (named in the tag, often a CVE).
scan_http_vulnerable.why: Patch or remove; these are actively targeted.

scan_ics.title: Accessible ICS Report
scan_ics.def: Industrial control systems (ICS/OT protocols such as Modbus or BACnet) reachable from the internet.
scan_ics.why: Can affect physical processes; must not be public.

scan_imap.title: Accessible IMAP Report
scan_imap.def: Mail servers with IMAP (143/tcp or 993/tcp) reachable from the internet, with their TLS details.
scan_imap.why: Normal for mail servers; check for old TLS and clear-text logins.

scan_ip_tunnel.title: Open IP-Tunnel Report
scan_ip_tunnel.def: Hosts that accept tunnelling packets (IPIP, GRE and similar) from anyone.
scan_ip_tunnel.why: Can be abused for spoofing and DoS; filter tunnel traffic.

scan_ipmi.title: Open IPMI Report
scan_ipmi.def: Server management controllers (IPMI, 623/udp) reachable from the internet.
scan_ipmi.why: Gives low-level control of the server; keep on a management network.

scan_ipp.title: Open IPP Report
scan_ipp.def: Printers with the Internet Printing Protocol (631/tcp) open to anyone.
scan_ipp.why: Can be abused and has had critical flaws; do not expose printers.

scan_isakmp.title: Vulnerable ISAKMP Report
scan_isakmp.def: VPN gateways with an IKE service that has a known weakness.

scan_kubernetes.title: Accessible Kubernetes API Server Report
scan_kubernetes.def: Kubernetes API servers reachable from the internet.
scan_kubernetes.why: Controls the whole cluster; restrict access.

scan_ldap_tcp.title: Open LDAP TCP Report
scan_ldap_tcp.def: Directory servers (LDAP 389/tcp or LDAPS 636/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_ldap_tcp.why: May leak directory data; keep internal.

scan_ldap_udp.title: Open LDAP Report
scan_ldap_udp.def: Directory servers answering LDAP on 389/udp from the internet.

scan_loop_dos.title: Loop DoS Report
scan_loop_dos.def: Services that can be tricked into endless reply loops with another service (application-layer loop DoS).
scan_loop_dos.why: Can be used to overload networks; update or restrict the service.

scan_mdns.title: Open mDNS Report
scan_mdns.def: Hosts answering multicast DNS (5353/udp) from the internet.
scan_mdns.why: Leaks device details and can amplify DDoS.

scan_memcached.title: Open Memcached Report
scan_memcached.def: Memcached caches reachable from the internet.

scan_mikrotik_service.title: Accessible MikroTik Service Report
scan_mikrotik_service.def: MikroTik routers answering the bandwidth test (btest) or WinBox management service from the internet.
scan_mikrotik_service.why: MikroTik routers are popular botnet targets; restrict management access and update RouterOS.

scan_mongodb.title: Open MongoDB Report
scan_mongodb.def: MongoDB databases (27017/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_mongodb.why: Often leaked or held to ransom; restrict access.

scan_mqtt.title: Open MQTT Report
scan_mqtt.def: IoT message brokers (MQTT 1883/8883) reachable from the internet, including ones without login.
scan_mqtt.why: May expose or allow control of IoT devices.

scan_msrpc.title: Accessible MS-RPC Service Report
scan_msrpc.def: Windows RPC services (for example 135/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_msrpc.why: Should never be public; a common attack path.

scan_mssql.title: Open MS-SQL Server Resolution Service Report
scan_mssql.def: Microsoft SQL Server browser service (1434/udp) reachable from the internet.
scan_mssql.why: Reveals database servers and can amplify DDoS.

scan_mysql.title: Accessible MySQL Server Report
scan_mysql.def: MySQL databases (3306/tcp) answering from the internet.

scan_nat_pmp.title: Open NAT-PMP Report
scan_nat_pmp.def: Routers answering NAT port mapping requests from the internet.
scan_nat_pmp.why: Can let outsiders change router port forwarding.

scan_netbios.title: Open NetBIOS Report
scan_netbios.def: Hosts answering Windows NetBIOS name requests from the internet.
scan_netbios.why: Leaks system details and can amplify DDoS.

scan_ntp.title: NTP Version Report
scan_ntp.def: Time servers (NTP) that answer version queries and can amplify DDoS.
scan_ntp.why: Restrict queries in the NTP configuration.

scan_ntpmonitor.title: NTP Monitor Report
scan_ntpmonitor.def: Time servers answering the 'monlist' query, a strong DDoS amplifier.

scan_pop3.title: Accessible POP3 Report
scan_pop3.def: Mail servers with POP3 (110/tcp or 995/tcp) reachable from the internet, with their TLS details.
scan_pop3.why: Normal for mail servers; check for old TLS and clear-text logins.

scan_portmapper.title: Open Portmapper Report
scan_portmapper.def: Hosts with the RPC portmapper (111) reachable from the internet.

scan_postgres.title: Accessible PostgreSQL Server Report
scan_postgres.def: PostgreSQL databases (5432/tcp) reachable from the internet.

scan_qotd.title: Open QOTD Report
scan_qotd.def: Hosts running the old Quote of the Day service on the internet.
scan_qotd.why: Used for DDoS amplification; switch it off.

scan_quic.title: Accessible QUIC Report
scan_quic.def: Services using the QUIC transport reachable from the internet.

scan_radmin.title: Accessible Radmin Report
scan_radmin.def: Radmin remote control services (4899/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_radmin.why: Remote access tools are prime targets; put them behind a VPN.

scan_rdp.title: Accessible RDP Report
scan_rdp.def: Windows Remote Desktop (RDP) reachable from the internet.
scan_rdp.why: A leading ransomware entry point; put RDP behind a VPN.

scan_rdpeudp.title: Accessible MS-RDPEUDP Report
scan_rdpeudp.def: Remote Desktop over UDP (3389/udp) reachable from the internet.
scan_rdpeudp.why: Exposes RDP and can amplify DDoS.

scan_redis.title: Open Redis Report
scan_redis.def: Redis databases reachable from the internet without a password.
scan_redis.why: Often taken over to run code; restrict immediately.

scan_rsync.title: Accessible Rsync Report
scan_rsync.def: rsync file services reachable from the internet without a password.

scan_sip.title: Accessible SIP Report
scan_sip.def: VoIP (SIP) services reachable from the internet.
scan_sip.why: Targeted for toll fraud; restrict access.

scan_slp.title: Accessible SLP Service Report
scan_slp.def: Service Location Protocol (427) reachable from the internet.
scan_slp.why: Very high DDoS amplification and known flaws.

scan_smb.title: Accessible SMB Report
scan_smb.def: Windows file sharing (SMB, 445/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_smb.why: A favourite target of worms and ransomware; block it at the border.

scan_smtp.title: Accessible SMTP Report
scan_smtp.def: Mail transfer servers (SMTP) reachable from the internet, with their TLS details.
scan_smtp.why: Normal for mail servers; check for open relays and old TLS.

scan_snmp.title: Open SNMP Report
scan_snmp.def: Devices answering SNMP with the default 'public' community from the internet.

scan_socks.title: Accessible SOCKS 4/5 Proxy Report
scan_socks.def: SOCKS proxies (1080/tcp) reachable from the internet.
scan_socks.why: Can be abused to relay attacks.

scan_ssdp.title: Open SSDP Report
scan_ssdp.def: Devices answering UPnP discovery (SSDP, 1900/udp) from the internet.
scan_ssdp.why: A common DDoS amplifier; disable UPnP on the WAN side.

scan_ssh.title: Accessible SSH Report
scan_ssh.def: SSH servers reachable from the internet, with software version and supported algorithms.
scan_ssh.why: Check for outdated versions and weaknesses such as Terrapin (CVE-2023-48795).

scan_ssl.title: Accessible SSL Report
scan_ssl.def: SSL/TLS services reachable from the internet, with certificate and encryption details.
scan_ssl.why: Look for expired or self-signed certificates and VPN or admin portals.

scan_ssl_freak.title: SSL FREAK Report
scan_ssl_freak.def: Servers that still accept weak 'export-grade' RSA ciphers (FREAK).

scan_ssl_poodle.title: SSL POODLE Report
scan_ssl_poodle.def: Servers that still accept SSL 3.0, which is open to the POODLE attack.

scan_stun.title: Accessible STUN Service Report
scan_stun.def: STUN servers (3478/udp, used by VoIP and video calls) reachable from the internet.

scan_telnet.title: Accessible Telnet Report
scan_telnet.def: Telnet logins (23/tcp and others) reachable from the internet.
scan_telnet.why: Clear-text logins and a top botnet target; disable Telnet.

scan_tftp.title: Open TFTP Report
scan_tftp.def: TFTP file services reachable from the internet.

scan_ubiquiti.title: Open Ubiquiti Report
scan_ubiquiti.def: Ubiquiti devices answering their discovery service (10001/udp) from the internet.
scan_ubiquiti.why: Leaks device details and amplifies DDoS.

scan_vnc.title: Accessible VNC Report
scan_vnc.def: VNC remote desktop services reachable from the internet.
scan_vnc.why: Remote screens are often weakly protected; restrict access.

scan_ws_discovery.title: Accessible WS-Discovery Service Report
scan_ws_discovery.def: Devices answering WS-Discovery (3702/udp, printers and cameras) from the internet.

scan_xdmcp.title: Accessible XDMCP Service Report
scan_xdmcp.def: X display managers (XDMCP) reachable from the internet.

_verified: 2026-11-07: every collection was matched to its report by file name (MongoDB filename / category = collection name) and the 'Filename' line on Shadowserver's report page. population_bgp is the population variant of scan_bgp; scan_mikrotik_service is listed as 'scan_miktrotik_service' (typo) on Shadowserver's page; the NTRIP and Radmin pages list no file name.
